subject: cul-tf-s
title: CUL.TF.S.------C.CONT.
description: Diagram in WAC-21, on the page where Braxton points to the effects of composers like Debussy in Europe or Harrison in America for understanding how actual cross-sectional extension would actualize, and where he argues 'the future of a given extension is directly related to whether or not that extension can absorb the multi-informational and vibrational demands that relate to composite continuance.' (C)CUL-TF-S (cultural transfer shifts) is crossed with C-CONT (composite continuance): the question is what cultural transfer shifts have to do with composite continuance — i.e., whether borrowed cross-cultural material can hold the line of a tradition rather than fragmenting it. CUL-TF-S outputs to TRS (transition) and C-CONT (the crossing). TRS then feeds INFO-CON (information convergence) → PROJ-DY (projectional dynamics). PROJ-DY branches to P-PART → T-C-IMP (time continuum implications) and to (R)ATTN (the reality of attraction) → AFL-DY (affinity dynamics) → RE-ST (restructuralism).
